newsitem.title: TANZANIA: World Food Programme warns of Tanzania famine.
newsitem.headline: World Food Programme warns of Tanzania famine.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) appealed on Tuesday for urgent food aid to avert a famine in Tanzania this year because of dismal crops in most of the country.
"Action to mobilise food imports, commercial or aid, is needed now if severe food shortages and famine are to be averted," said WFP in a report prepared for a donors' meeting.

"As a result of dismal production in most parts of the country it is envisaged that some parts will face severe food shortages and possibly famine, particularly during the period between September and January (1998), when harvests from the short rains are expected," it added.
It said WFP assessment teams had reported that migration had started from many villages hit by food shortages in Tanzania.
Tanzania's government Strategic Grain Reserve (SGR) had fallen to an unprecedented low of 17,000 tonnes, WFP added.
It said a joint Tanzanian government and U.N. agencies' mission to nine regions of Tanzania in late July showed the maize crop was poor with total failure in some prominent areas.
It said other usually productive areas expected a third of the usual maize crop and a large shortfall of food was expected to hit Tanzania between this September and April next year.

"Allocations, both from the government and WFP, are not sufficient for the most vulnerable people during the next four to eight months," said WFP, adding that WFP food donated for 200,000 people was now being shared among a much larger number.
East Africa suffered from a severe drought which largely ended in April with the start of the "long rains" season. But WFP said the rains, which stopped last month, were well below average.
